bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion alongside roughly 90% gross margins indicates improving product economics as commercialization develops. If this margin profile persists, incremental sales could contribute meaningfully toward fixed costs and support reinvestment, although profitability is not yet established.

Five ex-U.S. commercialization partners span more than 20 countries, while nine regulatory submissions are under review. This broadens potential market access and creates multiple regional pathways for adoption and licensing, reducing reliance on a single geography as approvals progress.

A cash balance of approximately $220M provides financial capacity to continue commercialization and regulatory efforts without the immediate burden of significant debt. Combined with minimal leverage, this supports operational flexibility, though continued losses could reduce that cushion over time.

bear.b: Large operating and free-cash-flow deficits show that the business is not yet self-funding despite growing revenue. Continued cash burn can constrain investment choices and increase dependence on external financing, particularly if commercialization takes longer or requires greater spending.

The wide gap between product sales and operating expenses demonstrates that early commercialization has not yet reached the scale needed to absorb the cost base. Until revenue grows materially or spending is reduced, operating leverage remains unfavorable and losses are likely to persist.

Weak retail adoption limits the breadth of the commercial channel and reduces visibility into repeat purchasing outside e-pharmacy. This may slow patient acquisition and make it harder to validate broad, durable demand across distribution channels during the next several months.
